# Three Dividend-paying Connectivity Investments to Buy


By:[Paul Dykewicz](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/author/pdykewicz-admin/)


, September 18, 2026


Link copied!


Three dividend-paying[connectivity investments](https://www.stockinvestor.com/three-connectivity-stocks-to-buy-for-profiting-from-ai/) to buy capitalize on AI by helping computers, software and devices link to the internet or communicate with each other to transfer data.


Top head of dividend-paying and connectivity giant AT&T Inc. (NYSE: T) was among the corporate executives who spoke about artificial intelligence (AI) at a Tuesday, Sept. 15, event in Washington, D.C. organized by the Business Roundtable to discuss how the technology can create new career opportunities rather than contribute to job cuts. The event, called “2026 CEO Workforce Forum: The New World of Work,” featured the views of John Stankey, chairman of the board and chief executive officer at AT&T Inc., among more than half a dozen top executives who presented.


Stankey appeared along with one of his AT&T managers, Associate Director of Network Process & Quality Jared Ridley, to address how workers at their company can use AI to aid their career development. Ridley said workers seize opportunities to tap the potential of AI to avoid becoming “stagnant.” “Keep learning” and appreciate the rewarding opportunity to use technology advances that arise, the manager added.


*AT&T manager Jared Ridley and CEO John Stankey discuss AI.*


Elsewhere on Sept. 15, Sam Altman, who has been the chief executive officer of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI since 2019, said “[the world should trust](https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cm70d91rg7l4t?post=asset%3A067e9270-7eaf-4e7a-a7e1-d653e474837a#post) ” AI companies to do what is right to contain the technology’s risks. However, lawmakers and activists gathered in Washington, D.C., for what they described as a “Pro-Human Assembly” in a subterranean conference center and Marriott Hotel ballroom in Washington, D.C., just blocks away from the White House, urging increased control of AI development and models.


Aside from the lively commentary about AI, the Federal Reserve held a policy meeting Sept. 15-16, and opted to raise rates 0.25% to curb stubborn inflation. Another 0.25% rate risk could take place later this year, its leaders indicated.


As usual, rate hikes lead to a decline in the share prices of stocks, and that happened on Wednesday afternoon, Sept. 16, after the Fed’s rate cut announcement. But the the market bounced back the following day as if the reaction to the news was overblown.


**Three Dividend-paying Connectivity Investments to Buy: T**


Dallas-based AT&T Inc. (NYSE: T) delivered improved second-quarter 2026 results and reaffirmed its multi-year guidance, wrote Citi Research. AT&T’s results reflected an expanding fiber total addressable market (TAM), deeper converged service penetration and favorable operating leverage partly from efficiency initiatives, the investment firm added.


The telecommunications company’s results also reflect a more active employment of back book pricing actions, while expanding its promotional menu to improve its share within the value segment, Citi Research opined. The combination of favorable volume and better wireless service revenue growth should help AT&T meet its high-level advanced connectivity revenue growth of at least 5% and generate significantly better EBITDA growth, according to the analysis.


Once again, the entry of Starlink into the mobile category of telecommunications poses a risk to long-term industry structure and terminal value that may limit upside potential for at least the near-term, according to Citi Research. The investment firm’s valuation methods reflect some of this uncertainty, contributing to a reduced price target of $28 for AT&T.

T is a former recommendation of Bryan Perry in his[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) investment newsletter. His subscribers were able to notch a 34.19% gain between when he advised to buy it on November 10, 2023, and its sale date of April 1, 2025. If the company’s share price dips, it would not surprise me if he took a fresh look at it on a reduced valuation.


*Bryan Perry heads the[Cash Machine](https://www.bryanperryinvesting.com/offer/cash-default/?source=GURUCASH1) newsletter.*

**Three Dividend-paying Connectivity Investments to Buy: VZ**


Verizon, the world’s second-largest telecommunications company by revenue and the largest wireless carrier in the United States, is another connectivity stock to consider. It entered the artificial intelligence infrastructure market with an announcement during its Q2 2026 earnings call that it agreed to a $1 billion-plus dark fiber deal with Google, part of Mountain View, California-based Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG). The pact led to upgraded, full-year financial guidance for Verizon and an expanding strategy to retrofit central offices for artificial intelligence (AI) workloads.


Risk exists that cost cutting could have an unintended consequence on future operating performance, Citi Research commented. However, the investment firm maintained its Buy rating on Verizon with an unchanged target.


Citi Research plans to look further into the potential sources of upside in Verizon’s wireless wholesale revenue during the second quarter of 2026 relative to its estimates, Rollins wrote. His earnings per share (EPS) for 2026 is unchanged at $5.01, while incorporating some dilution in 2027 partly from a recently disclosed spectrum purchase.


“We believe the wireless competitive landscape is showing some positive signs of stabilizing over the near term, while Verizon is enhancing its go-to-market position with its refreshed rate plans, converged offers and small rebound in core prepaid,” Rollins wrote. “However, the larger question and risk that is still orbiting around the telco and cable stocks is the possibility that LEO \[low-Earth-orbit\] satellite constellations, including StarLink, become a direct and broader competitor to both wireless and broadband in the U.S. market.”

**Three Dividend-paying Connectivity Investments to Buy: IXP**


iShares Global Communication Services ETF (NYSE Arca: IXP) is a fund favored by Michelle Connell, founder and chief investment officer with Dallas-based[Portia Capital Management](https://www.portia-capital-management.com/) . The ETF provides investors global exposure to telecommunications media and digital entertainment companies.


*Michelle Connell heads[Portia Capital Management](https://www.portia-capital-management.com/) .*


Advertisement.


“In addition to traditional communication companies, such as AT&T and Verizon, IXP also holds positions in digital media titans such as Disney and Netflix, as well as positions in hyperscalers such as Meta and Alphabet,” Connell said. “Thus, this ETF’s diversity provides investment in all facets of communication services.”


In addition to this industry diversity, IXP also provides global exposure to communication services outside of United States, Connell continued. Currently, 19% of the ETFs companies domicile in Asia. Plus, 10% of its holdings are European. This diversification will not only provide IXP exposure to communication services’ technologies developed overseas, but also provide participation in markets where the birth rates are high, she added.


Income investors should like the fund’s dividend. IXP currently pays a dividend yield of 3.31%.
